title: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 + fused ops, rotary/ROPE support, KV continuous batching & scheduler tweaks
author: Daniel Park
description:
Motivation: Reduce per-token latency and cost for long-context chat workloads by migrating our custom attention implementation to FlashAttentionV2 variants, enabling fused rotary/ROPE ops, and improving KV cache continuous batching and scheduler heuristics. This PR combines kernel upgrades with small runtime changes to make fused attention kernels the default on supported NVidia architectures and to fall back gracefully.

Changes: - Integrate FlashAttentionV2 kernels with support for both rotary and ROPE positional encodings (selectable via model metadata). - Add fused query/key/value fused ops path for common transformer blocks to reduce memory bandwidth. - Implement continuous KV batching: persistent KV queues that allow background batching of tail requests without increasing p99 latency. - Scheduler tweaks: request shaping and quick-fallback policy to route requests to compatible model variants if fused kernels not available. - KV cache manager improvements: thread-safe eviction, async prefetch on rollouts, and memory accounting to avoid OOM on large contexts. - Add microbenchmarks, unit tests, and perf harness changes to validate throughput/latency.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel integration and API wiring
- [x] Fallback paths for unsupported GPUs
- [x] Scheduler policy updates and config toggles
- [x] KV caching correctness and concurrency tests
- [x] Benchmarks showing >1.6x throughput on A100 for 8k contexts
- [x] Release notes entry and migration guide

Related: ENG-3245 (attention performance epic), ENG-3310 (kv batching design). Notes: This is a behavior-preserving change for model outputs; numerical differences are within expected floating-point tolerances. Always enable via runtime feature gate until rollout is complete.
commit_summary: feat(attention): add FlashAttentionV2 kernel backend with rotary/ROPE support
perf(attention): implement fused qkv op and reduce memcpy paths
runtime(kv): continuous batching queue and background batch worker
runtime(scheduler): add fallback routing policy and quick-shape heuristics
tests: add microbenchmarks for A100 and T4, add KV concurrency tests
docs: add changelog entry and migration guide
review_comments: Priya Sharma: This looks great overall. A couple questions: 1) Do we have a rollout plan to avoid perf cliffs on mixed GPU clusters? 2) Can you add a feature gate flag in the console to toggle fused ops per-tenant?
Daniel Park (author): Answered: Added scheduler routing to prefer nodes with feature flag and added per-tenant runtime flag; rollout plan documented in the PR description under 'Notes'.
Alex Gomez: Observed small numerical diffs in the unit tests for the 16-bit path. Are these within tolerance?
Daniel Park (author): Confirmed: diffs are <0.02% relative for most logits; added additional fp16 normalization and an optional deterministic path for exact-match tests.
Kai Huang: CI perf-bench showed a small regression on T4 for 2k contexts in the first run. Can we get another run after the KV queue backpressure fix?
Daniel Park (author): Re-ran perf suite after backpressure fix; T4 numbers recovered and A100 saw 1.6x throughput improvement for 8k contexts. Updated perf results in the PR comments.
ci_checks: perf-bench: initial run flaky on T4 -> rerun -> pass, A100 throughput +60%@8k context
release_notes: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused QKV and rotary/ROPE support. Enables continuous KV batching and scheduler improvements. Expected impact: ~1.6x throughput on A100 for long-context workloads, reduced per-token cost. Gradual rollout behind feature gates; no breaking changes to API.
